title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability
author: Anika Patel
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with expected client behavior. This PR consolidates param handling (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty), consistent role handling for assistant/system/user messages, signal/stop token support, returning logprobs where requested, and improvements to response formatting (structured output / content-type mapping) and streaming stability for function/tool call flows.

Summary of changes: consolidated request parsing to a single compatibility adapter, unified role mapping with explicit validation and error messages, implemented stop token semantics at both tokenizer and stream boundaries, plumbed logprobs support through the decoder path, normalized the response formatting step to produce OpenAI-like choices/usage objects, and hardened the streaming path to ensure deterministic chunking for function/tool calls (including stable function call JSON object emission).

Backward/forward compatibility: default behavior is unchanged for Redwood-native clients. OpenAI compatibility mode is opt-in via an API flag (compat=openai). Carefully scoped codepaths minimize perf impact; key perf-sensitive paths were bench-marked and minor optimizations were added to mitigate overhead. No breaking changes to existing Redwood API surface are expected, but customers using the compatibility flag should verify stop token edge cases noted below.

Testing and validation: unit tests for param parsing and role translation, integration tests against the eval-harness OpenAI-compat test suite (message/role permutations, stop sequences, top_p and temperature combinations), streaming canary tests run against perf-canary infra, and manual verification with official OpenAI SDKs to validate response shape.

Risk and rollout: feature gated behind compat=openai. Will rollout as a staged canary: 5% (internal), 25% (beta customers), 100% opt-in. Post-merge jobs will create a migration note and example snippets in redwood-docs.

Checklist: [x] param parsing [x] roles mapping [x] stop tokens in sync with tokenizer and stream [x] logprobs plumbing [x] response formatting consistent with OpenAI shape [x] streaming stability for tool/function calls [x] tests + canary runs

review_comments: Diego Ramos (reviewer): Can you call out where we validate mixed role sequences (e.g., system appearing mid-conversation)? Need explicit error behavior documented.
Author (Anika): Addressed — added explicit validation in server/runtime/roles.py and documented the error and the auto-normalization behavior in openai_compat.md.
Lena Fischer (reviewer): Streaming chunks sometimes split JSON objects for function calls in internal canary. How did you address the boundary issue?

Author (Anika): Streaming boundary fix: we buffer until the function call object is complete or a max chunk size is reached; added tests in tests/compat/test_streaming_function_calls.py and a perf regression check. Verified behavior with the Node SDK.

See docs/openai_compat.md for migration and examples.
